Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

18:1740-1977 



Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
FLAT COTTON WICKS 

( First Revision ) 



(Reaffirmed 2002) 



1. Scope — Covers flat cotton wicks (6 to 25 mm wide) for use in hurricane lanterns and lamps. 

2. Manufacture 

2.1 Yarn — Soft spun and reasonably clean and free from leaf particles, neps, snarls, slubs and other 
defects. 



2.1.1 Approximate count of yarn for manufacturers' guidance 

Warp 



Face and Back 
68/3(or98 tex x 3) 



Selvedge and Binding 
10B/2(or60texx 2) 



Weft 



30s/2(or20 tex X 2) 



2.2 ly/cA — Woven in double plain yveave, uniform in thickness and width and free from weaving 
defects as far as practicable, and ajs^o free from sizing and finishing materials. 

3. Requirements-— See Tables 1 and 2.

4. Packing — Preferably into 10 m rolls, each roil being wrapped in waterproof paper. 

5, Marking — Each roll of wick shall be attached with a tag giving the following information: 

a) Name of the material; 

b) Size number; 

c) Length in metres; 

d) Manufacturer's name, initials or trade-mark, if any; and 

e) Month and year of manufacture. 

5.1 Certification Mariiing — Details available with the Bureau of Indian Standards.

APPENDIX A 

[ Table 2, Item (iii) ] 
METHOD OF TEST FOR OIL ABSORPTION TIME 
A-1. Cut from each roll in the test sample one specimen measuring approximately 15 cm. 

A-2. Take a beaker and a stand. 

A-3. Take one test specimen and place two marks / and Y on it at 5 and 10 cm respectively from one 
of its ends. Suspend the test specimen from the other end vertically in a beaker containing kerosine 
[ see IS : 1459-1974 Specification for kerosine ( second revision ) ] up to a height of 8 cm so that the 
mark / on the test specimen is just submerged In oil (see Fig. 1 ). Note the time taken by the 
kerosine to rise up to mark K.
